title: Home Mortgage Loans Origination Standard: Underwriting Authority, Note Rate, Funding and Escrow at Closing
content:
This standard governs how a Home Mortgage Loans application is approved, priced, funded and set up for escrow at closing.

## Underwriting authority

Underwriting approves a loan only within the requested program's smallest and largest loan amount, its largest loan-to-value, its lowest credit score, its highest debt-to-income ratio and its eligible occupancy types. These are credit decisions made by the underwriting system, and never by the agent.

## The note rate

The note rate is the program's published note rate, locked for the program's lock period.

## Funding

The loan funds at closing with one disbursement of the loan proceeds. That disbursement includes any upfront insurance premium the program finances, taken as the program's upfront percent of the base loan amount.

## The first installment

The first installment is due on the program's due day of the month, in the month falling the program's stated number of calendar months after the month in which the loan funded.

## Escrow at closing

An escrow account is required when the original loan-to-value exceeds the program's escrow threshold, and on a program marked as always requiring escrow it is required on every loan whatever the original loan-to-value. Where escrow is not required on that basis, the borrower may waive it by paying the program's escrow waiver fee, taken as a percent of the loan, at closing.

## Condition and result

| Condition at closing | Result |
|---|---|
| The program requires escrow on every loan | An escrow account is set up |
| The original loan-to-value exceeds the program's escrow threshold | An escrow account is set up |
| Neither holds, and the borrower waives escrow | The program's waiver fee is paid at closing, as a percent of the loan |

The escrow threshold is a boundary of exceeding, so an original loan-to-value standing exactly at the program's threshold figure does not of itself require an escrow account, while one standing above it does.
